stem: A client with chronic right-sided heart failure has jugular venous distention, bilateral dependent edema, and abdominal fullness. Which pathophysiologic change best explains this cluster of findings?

options.A: Systemic venous blood backs up because the right ventricle cannot move blood forward effectively.
options.B: Left atrial pressure rises and forces fluid primarily into the pulmonary alveoli.
options.C: Acute bronchial smooth-muscle constriction traps air in the distal airways.
options.D: Loss of plasma protein in the urine lowers oncotic pressure as the primary problem.

rationale: A is correct. In right-sided heart failure, impaired right-ventricular pumping causes blood returning from the body to back up in the systemic venous circulation. The resulting venous congestion contributes to jugular venous distention and fluid accumulation in dependent tissues and the abdomen. B describes the pulmonary-congestion mechanism more characteristic of left-sided failure. C describes obstructive airway physiology and does not explain systemic venous distention. D can cause generalized edema in nephrotic states but does not explain the right-heart-failure pattern of jugular venous congestion in this stem.
educational_objective: Link jugular venous distention, dependent edema, and abdominal congestion in right-sided heart failure to impaired right-ventricular forward flow and systemic venous backup.
source_document_title: Types of Heart Failure; Heart Failure Signs and Symptoms
source_version_date: Last reviewed May 21 and May 29, 2025; accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Types of Heart Failure — right-sided heart failure: when the right side loses pumping power, blood backs up in the veins; Heart Failure Signs and Symptoms — edema/weight gain from venous backup and fluid movement into tissues
source_claim_supported: Right-sided heart failure causes systemic venous backup and congestion, producing findings such as peripheral/abdominal edema; venous congestion is mechanistically distinct from pulmonary alveolar congestion caused by elevated left-sided filling pressures.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation, page 14; activity statements: ‘Identify pathophysiology related to an acute or chronic condition’ and ‘Manage the care of a client with alteration in hemodynamics, tissue perfusion and hemostasis’
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — right-sided heart failure and systemic venous congestion
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source recognition item to avoid duplicating V2-Q1405’s complication-identification construct. The final item tests the mechanism linking a realistic right-heart-failure assessment cluster to systemic venous congestion, with physiologically plausible alternative mechanisms.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: right-sided heart failure / systemic venous congestion
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current AHA heart-failure materials. AHA specifically explains that loss of right-sided pumping power causes blood to back up in the veins and links venous backup to tissue edema.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: The stem uses a coherent right-heart-failure congestion cluster. A directly states the supported mechanism. B, C, and D are real alternative mechanisms that can produce cardiopulmonary or edema findings but do not best explain the complete stem.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct. Impaired right-ventricular forward flow produces systemic venous backup and congestion.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect. Elevated left atrial pressure primarily produces pulmonary venous/alveolar congestion and does not best explain the systemic venous cluster.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect. Bronchoconstriction causes airflow obstruction, not jugular venous distention with dependent systemic edema.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect. Low oncotic pressure from urinary protein loss can cause edema but does not account for the stated chronic right-sided heart failure and jugular venous congestion.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A explains all findings while remaining anchored to the established diagnosis. D can produce edema but not the full systemic venous-congestion pattern; B and C describe different organ-system mechanisms.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are mechanistic explanations of similar grammatical structure and comparable detail.
audit_findings.blueprint: Directly aligned with 2026 Physiological Adaptation pathophysiology and hemodynamics activity statements.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Re-audited for right-versus-left heart failure physiology, edema differentials, JVD specificity, causal wording, overlap with V2-Q1405, distractor plausibility, and NCLEX application level. No unresolved conflict remained.
